speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I’m Dr. Agent. Can you tell me exactly where the wrist pain is located and how long you’ve been experiencing the fever and skin lesions?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient presents with a 3-day history of pain in his left wrist, which worsened this morning accompanied by chills and malaise. He recounts having a self-resolving left knee pain the previous week. Reports recent return from a camping trip in Minnesota. Sexually active with one female partner. No history of trauma to the wrist.

speaker: Doctor
text: Did you notice a red, expanding rash or a tick bite during your camping trip in Minnesota, and have you observed any other joint swelling since the knee pain? REQUEST IMAGES

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Pain in the left wrist. I also have Chills, Malaise, Painless violaceous vesiculopustular lesions on both wrists and hands, Swelling and erythema of the left wrist, Severe tenderness to palpation and passive movement of the left wrist.

speaker: Doctor
text: The description of painless violaceous vesiculopustular lesions on the hands and wrists, especially after a camping trip in an endemic area, is highly suggestive of Hand, Foot, and Mouth Disease variant or potentially Rocky Mountain Spotted Fever, but the migratory arthritis points elsewhere. Let me check for other systemic signs. Do you have any headache, rash on your palms or soles, or a history of a bull's-eye rash? REQUEST TEST: Lyme disease serology

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the recent travel to Minnesota, migratory joint pain, and characteristic violaceous vesiculopustular lesions on the hands, this clinical picture is highly suggestive of Colorado Tick Fever. REQUEST TEST: Colorado Tick Fever PCR

speaker: Doctor
text: The normal Lyme and Colorado Tick Fever results, combined with the specific violaceous vesiculopustular lesions on the hands and wrists after camping in Minnesota, strongly point to a different vector-borne illness. I suspect this may be St. Louis Encephalitis or another flavivirus, but the arthritis is prominent. Let me rule out other common arboviruses. REQUEST TEST: West Nile Virus IgM

speaker: Doctor
text: With Lyme, Colorado Tick Fever, and West Nile ruled out, I need to reconsider the differential for a tick-borne illness in Minnesota that causes migratory arthritis and a vesicular rash. REQUEST TEST: Anaplasma phagocytophilum PCR

speaker: Doctor
text: The normal results for Lyme, Colorado Tick Fever, West Nile, and Anaplasma make typical vector-borne diseases unlikely, so I need to consider non-tick transmitted causes like disseminated gonococcal infection given your sexual history. Do you have any history of genital ulcers, discharge, or pain during urination? REQUEST TEST: Gonococcus PCR

speaker: Doctor
text: The positive Gonococcus PCR confirms Disseminated Gonococcal Infection, which explains the migratory arthritis and characteristic vesiculopustular skin lesions. DIAGNOSIS READY: Disseminated Gonococcal Infection
